title: Etale-chart derived base change for the infinitesimal module limit
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Separated, finite type and proper morphisms use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finitely presented on etale scheme charts. Use quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it has a presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to F\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Base-flatness means flatness of stalks on etale scheme charts over the corresponding local rings of the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Proper support means there exist a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z$ proper over the base and a finite type quasi-coherent module $G$ on $Z$ such that $i_*G\simeq F$ [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Let $(A_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse sequence of commutative rings with surjective transition maps whose kernels are locally nilpotent, meaning every element of each kernel is nilpotent, and set $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated and finitely presented, put $X_n=X\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A_n$. For every $n\geq1$ let $M_n$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-module, flat over $A_n$, with support proper over $A_n$, with specified isomorphisms $M_n\otimes_{A_n}A_{n-1}\simeq M_{n-1}$ for $n\geq2$. Use unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology. Regard $M_n$ as a module on $X$ by direct image along $X_n\hookrightarrow X$; the given transition isomorphisms followed by quotient maps define its inverse-system maps. The symbol $R\varprojlim_{D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}}M_n$ denotes the homotopy inverse limit in this full derived subcategory: it fits into the product triangle $K\to\prod_{n\geq1}M_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod_{n\geq1}M_n\to K[1]$, with products taken in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ and projections $q_n:K\to M_n$ induced by the first arrow. Here the shift has $n$th component equal to the transition map composed with the $(n+1)$st projection. Let $K$ be this homotopy inverse limit [lem-sfb-space-inverse-module-derived-limit]. For every quasi-compact quasi-separated etale scheme chart $U\to X$ and every $n\geq1$, put $U_n=U\times_X X_n$. The morphism induced by the projection $q_n$ and scalar extension is an isomorphism in $D(A_n)$: $$R\Gamma(U,K)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(U_n,M_n|_{U_n}).$$ These are the projection-induced morphisms, not arbitrary isomorphisms. They commute with restriction of etale charts and with the transition isomorphisms $M_n\otimes_{A_n}A_{n-1}\simeq M_{n-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0CX8 (lemma-compute-over-affine), with its canonical maps from 0CX6 (lemma-compute-against-perfect).

proof.text: Fix $u:U\to X$ and $n$. The derived-limit statement gives $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $q_{n-1}=t_nq_n$. The closed-immersion module statement gives $i_{n,*}M_n\in\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$. Put $L_n=i_{n,*}M_n$. It retains its commuting $A_n$-action. Apply the perfect-telescope statement to $u$, and write $T_m(L)=R\Gamma(X,E_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}L)$ and $S(L)=R\Gamma(U,u^*L)$. Its actual cocone maps give $\operatorname{hocolim}_mT_m(K)\simeq S(K)$ in $D(A)$ and $\operatorname{hocolim}_mT_m(L_n)\simeq S(L_n)$ in $D(A_n)$. The same $E_m$ work for both coefficients.

source.place: Tag 0CX8 (lemma-compute-over-affine), first and second paragraphs, using 0CX5 and 0CRW.

proof.text: Let $F_n=-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_n$. The derived change-of-rings statement makes $F_n$ exact; the normalized coefficient adjunction, on the one-object ringed site, makes it left adjoint to scalar restriction. Thus the left-adjoint colimit theorem gives preservation of countable coproducts. Apply the exact-functor telescope lemma: the scalar-extension comparison $\operatorname{hocolim}_m F_nT_m(K)\to F_nS(K)$ is an isomorphism. We use the telescope map induced on complex representatives, so its legs are $F_n(\theta_{m,K})$; no uniqueness of cone fillers is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0CX8 (lemma-compute-over-affine), final sentence: derived tensor commutes with homotopy colimits.

proof.text: For each $m$, apply the perfect-test statement to $E_m$, using the symmetry of tensor. It says that the scalar adjunct $F_nT_m(K)\to T_m(L_n)$ of $T_m(q_n)$ is an isomorphism in $D(A_n)$. Naturality in $E_m$ makes these a morphism of sequential diagrams. Applying the homotopy-colimit functor to this diagram isomorphism therefore gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{hocolim}_mF_nT_m(K)\to\operatorname{hocolim}_mT_m(L_n)$. Together with the two preceding steps this proves an isomorphism $F_nS(K)\to S(L_n)$.

source.place: Tag 0CX8 (lemma-compute-over-affine), last paragraph, applying 0CX6 to E_m.

proof.text: This isomorphism is the desired scalar adjunct, not a choice of an unrelated isomorphism. Indeed, write $\eta$ for the scalar-extension unit and $\beta_m$ for the maps of step 3. Their defining equations are $\operatorname{Res}(\beta_m)\eta=T_m(q_n)$. Naturality of the actual telescope cocones gives $S(q_n)\theta_{m,K}=\theta_{m,L_n}T_m(q_n)$. Apply scalar adjunction to this equality. Its left side transposes to the scalar adjunct of $S(q_n)$ composed with $F_n\theta_{m,K}$; its right side transposes to $\theta_{m,L_n}\beta_m$. The functorial telescope construction on complex representatives respects this equality and its transition maps, so the isomorphism of step 3 is exactly the scalar adjunct of $S(q_n)$. This uses naturality for the full diagram, not an inference that maps out of an arbitrary cone are determined by its individual legs.

source.place: Tag 0CX8 (lemma-compute-over-affine), functorial use of 0CRW and canonical maps of 0CX6.

proof.text: Identify the target. A representable closed immersion is affine on each scheme test. Affine higher-image vanishing gives $Ri_{n,*}M_n=i_{n,*}M_n$, with the canonical degree-zero comparison. The derived etale-chart comparison gives $u^*Ri_{n,*}M_n\simeq Rj_{n,*}(M_n|_{U_n})$, where $j_n:U_n\hookrightarrow U$. Apply the unbounded ringed-site Leray statement to $j_n$ and the terminal object of the small etale site of $U$. It identifies the underlying additive derived sections of $S(L_n)$ with those of $R\Gamma(U_n,M_n|_{U_n})$. Its comparison on representatives is the identity on sections and therefore respects the existing $A_n$-actions. Hence this is the canonical comparison in $D(A_n)$: restriction of scalars detects quasi-isomorphisms. Every map here is the restriction or derived-composition comparison, so the adjunct identified in step 4 is precisely the projection-induced map in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0CX8 (lemma-compute-over-affine), displayed first equality; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0D6G and 0D6E. Also Tag 0D6H (lemma-Leray-unbounded).

proof.text: For a map of etale charts $V\to U$ over $X$, the restriction square for $q_n$ commutes because $q_n$ is one fixed morphism on $X$. Taking its scalar adjunct preserves that square by naturality of the adjunction. Thus the maps just proved invertible commute with chart restriction, independently of which perfect telescope was used. Similarly $q_{n-1}=t_nq_n$ gives the transition square: after identifying $(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_n)\otimes_{A_n}^{\mathbf L}A_{n-1}$ with $C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_{n-1}$, both composite adjuncts are the adjunct of $t_nq_n$. The target's scalar-extension transition is the one induced by $M_n\otimes_{A_n}A_{n-1}\simeq M_{n-1}$; its derived version agrees since $M_n$ is flat over $A_n$. The perfect-test statement already supplies this same transition compatibility before taking telescopes. Consequently the computed projection-induced isomorphisms have both required compatibilities.
